title: Singly-even permutation equivalence in the Li-Kaleyski Theorem 1 family
summary: Determine whether a member of the fixed Li-Kaleyski Theorem 1 APN family can be CCZ-equivalent to a permutation in a singly-even dimension.

formal_statement.body: For $q=2^i$, let $F^{(1)}_{i,m}:\mathbb F_{2^m}^3\to\mathbb F_{2^m}^3$ be $F^{(1)}_{i,m}(x,y,z)=(x^{q+1}+x^qz+yz^q,\ x^qz+y^{q+1},\ xy^q+y^qz+z^{q+1})$, with the admissibility and APN hypotheses of source Theorem 1 and $\gcd(i,m)=1$. Decide whether there exist admissible $i,m$ with $3m\equiv2\pmod4$ such that $F^{(1)}_{i,m}$ is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation. Exhibit an explicit equivalence and permutation, or prove that none exists.

scope.domain: CCZ-equivalence to permutations within the fixed Theorem 1 trivariate APN family
assumptions: The function and polynomial root conditions are exactly those of source Theorem 1
$\gcd(i,m)=1$, so the admitted member is APN
The total binary dimension $3m$ is singly even
scope.unresolved_remainder: Doubly-even dimensions and the dimension-six case are excluded by source results. No inspected theorem decides CCZ-equivalence to a permutation for the fixed family in the remaining singly-even dimensions.

citations.label: Li--Kaleyski, Two New Infinite Families of APN Functions in Trivariate Form

progress.summary: The source leaves CCZ-equivalence of its Theorem 1 APN family to permutations in singly-even dimensions as a problem for future work.
